test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rohit Sharma __is better than more other batsman__ in the world.

options.text: as good as the most other batsman

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. better than most other batsmen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence compares Rohit Sharma with other batsmen in the world, making it a case of** comparative degree**.
 
• The phrase **"better than more other batsman"** is grammatically incorrect and needs substitution.
 
• The correct comparative form is **"better than most other batsmen"**, which appropriately compares Rohit Sharma to the majority of batsmen.

Correct sentence: *Rohit Sharma is **better than most other batsmen** in the world.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without comparison. Example: Rohit is a good batsman.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two entities. Example: Rohit is better than Virat.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Compares one entity with all others. Example: Rohit is the best batsman.
 
 
 
• **Option Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "the best batsmen" — Incorrect, as it changes the comparative degree to superlative.
 
• **Option 2:** "a better batsman" — Incorrect, as it doesn't compare Rohit to other batsmen.
 
• **Option 3:** "better than most other batsmen" — Correct, as it maintains the comparative degree and logical meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** "as good as the most other batsman" — Incorrect, as it changes the degree and meaning.
